Walter Rodney was a Guyanese historian and activist, author of How Europe Underdeveloped Africa (1972). He was killed by a bomb in Georgetown in 1980.

He studied African history in London and taught in Jamaica, which banned him in 1968, setting off riots, and in Tanzania. His book argued that Africa's poverty came from the slave trade and colonial rule, not from anything lacking in Africans. It was read across Africa and the Caribbean.

Back in Guyana, he helped found the Working People's Alliance, which joined Indian and African Guyanese against the government of Forbes Burnham. On 13 June 1980 a radio given to him exploded in his car. An inquiry in 2016 found that the state was behind his death. He is remembered with Cheddi Jagan as a voice of Caribbean freedom.
sum: Walter Rodney was a Guyanese historian and activist, author of How Europe Underdeveloped Africa (1972). He was killed by a bomb in Georgetown in 1980.
